3	Dependabot opens the PR. Upshift makes it pass.
4	
5	Upshift is an agent that fixes the code a version change breaks. Give it a Python repo and a package to
6	upgrade. It researches the upgrade itself (changelog, release notes, migration guide, and an API diff
7	made by installing both versions), writes a playbook where every rule cites its source, bumps the
8	dependency, fixes the code one root cause at a time, and proves nothing new broke against the test
9	baseline it recorded before touching anything.
10	
11	Built for #neatHack with neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai. Bring your own model key.
12	
13	## Status
14	
15	Day 1: the package-bump pipeline works end to end with model calls stubbed out. Vulnerability scans,
16	Python version bumps and third-party API drift come next.
17	
18	## Run it
19	
20	```bash
21	uv sync
22	python3 scripts/check_secrets.py --install   # pre-commit hook that blocks committed keys
23	cp .env.example .env                         # fill in your provider and key (git-ignored)
24	
25	# no model calls: clone, baseline, research, bump, and show what breaks
26	uv run upshift bump --repo demo/shop_app --package pydantic --to 2 --dry-run
27	
28	# the full agent
29	uv run upshift bump --repo demo/shop_app --package pydantic --to 2
30	uv run upshift resume <run-id>     # continue a crashed or killed run
31	```
32	
33	Runs live in `.upshift/runs/<run-id>/`: the working copy, its venv, `state.json`, the research sources and
34	the report. Playbooks are cached in `playbooks/` and reused by the next repo on the same upgrade.
35	
36	## Models: bring your own key
37	
38	Set `UPSHIFT_PROVIDER` and `UPSHIFT_MODEL` plus that provider's key in `.env` (read automatically,
39	never committed) or in your shell.
40	
41	| `UPSHIFT_PROVIDER` | Needs | Notes |
42	|---|---|---|
43	| `azure-openai` | `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY`, `AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` | `UPSHIFT_MODEL` is the deployment name |
44	| `openai` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Set `OPENAI_BASE_URL` for any OpenAI-compatible service (OpenRouter, Groq, Together, a local server) |
45	| `bedrock` | `UPSHIFT_AWS_PROFILE` | An explicit profile is required, so the default AWS account is never billed by accident |
46	
47	The agent uses one message format internally and each provider translates to it, so adding a
48	provider means one adapter in `upshift/llm.py`. Every client is wrapped with `neatlogs.wrap`, so
49	model calls are traced with tokens and latency whichever provider you pick.
50	
51	## How a job runs
52	
53	| Phase | What happens | Where the tools come in |
54	|---|---|---|
55	| setup | Clone, create a venv, install, resolve the target version from PyPI | |
56	| baseline | Run the tests before changing anything | `entire graph verify --record-baseline` |
57	| research | Docs, changelog, GitHub release notes, API diff of both installed versions → cited playbook | neatlogs `RETRIEVER`/`AGENT` spans |
58	| bump | Rewrite the pins and install the new version | |
59	| fix | One root cause per round. Progress is committed, regressions are reverted | `entire graph search / impact / explain` tools, one neatlogs span per round |
60	| verify | No new failures against the baseline, no old APIs left from the playbook | `entire graph verify --pre-edit-baseline` |
61	| report | `UPSHIFT_REPORT.md` with changes, verification and sources | |
62	
63	Every job is one neatlogs trace.
64	
65	## Tests
66	
67	```bash
68	uv run pytest
69	```
70	
71	The fix-loop tests drive the real loop (repo, venv, pytest, git) with a scripted model in place of a real one.

42	|---|---|---|

49	model calls are traced with tokens and latency whichever provider you pick.

54	|---|---|---|
55	| setup | Clone, create a venv, install, resolve the target version from PyPI | |
56	| baseline | Run the tests before changing anything | `entire graph verify --record-baseline` |
57	| research | Docs, changelog, GitHub release notes, API diff of both installed versions → cited playbook | neatlogs `RETRIEVER`/`AGENT` spans |
58	| bump | Rewrite the pins and install the new version | |
59	| fix | One root cause per round. Progress is committed, regressions are reverted | `entire graph search / impact / explain` tools, one neatlogs span per round |
60	| verify | No new failures against the baseline, no old APIs left from the playbook | `entire graph verify --pre-edit-baseline` |
61	| report | `UPSHIFT_REPORT.md` with changes, verification and sources | |
62	
63	Every job is one neatlogs trace.
64

68	uv run pytest
69	```

@.entire/graph-agent.md

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

class FixLoop:
    def __init__(self, ws: Workspace, llm, state: RunState, playbook: dict, max_rounds: int = 12):
        self.ws, self.llm, self.state, self.playbook = ws, llm, state, playbook
        self.max_rounds = max_rounds
        self.baseline = set(state.baseline_failing)
        self.system = SYSTEM.format(package=state.package, old=state.old, new=state.new,
                                    playbook=render_playbook(playbook))

    def new_failures(self, run: TestRun) -> set[str]:
        return run.failing - self.baseline

    def run(self, save) -> TestRun:
        current = self.ws.run_tests()
        stalls = 0
        while self.state.round < self.max_rounds:
            if not self.new_failures(current) and current.exit_code in (0, 1, 5):
                break
            self.state.round += 1
            current, outcome = self.one_round(self.state.round, current)
            save()
            stalls = stalls + 1 if outcome != "progress" else 0
            if stalls >= MAX_STALLS:
                self.state.notes.append(f"stopped after {stalls} rounds without progress")
                break
        return current

    def one_round(self, n: int, before: TestRun) -> tuple[TestRun, str]:
        with neatlogs.trace(f"fix.{n}", kind="AGENT") as span:
            failing = sorted(self.new_failures(before))
            prompt = (f"Round {n}. {len(failing)} tests fail that passed before the upgrade "
                      f"({before.passed} passing now).\nFailing: {', '.join(failing[:40])}\n\n"
                      f"Previous rounds:\n" + ("\n".join(self.state.round_log) or "(none)") +
                      f"\n\nPytest output:\n{tail(before.output, 10000)}")
            try:
                summary = self.converse(prompt)
            except LLMError as exc:
                code = exc.code
                tracing.annotate(failure_class=f"llm:{code}", recovery="revert_and_retry_next_round")
                self.ws.git("checkout", "--", ".")
                self.ws.git("clean", "-fdq")
                self.state.round_log.append(f"round {n}: model call failed ({code}); changes reverted")
                return before, "error"

            after = self.ws.run_tests()
            new_before, new_after = self.new_failures(before), self.new_failures(after)
            if after.passed < before.passed and len(new_after) >= len(new_before):
                outcome = "regression"
                self.ws.git("checkout", "--", ".")
                self.ws.git("clean", "-fdq")
                tracing.annotate(failure_class="test_regression", recovery="revert_and_replan")
                self.state.round_log.append(
                    f"round {n}: REVERTED. '{summary}' made things worse "
                    f"({before.passed} -> {after.passed} passing). Try a different approach.")
                after = before
            elif self.ws.git("status", "--porcelain").strip() and (
                    after.passed > before.passed or len(new_after) < len(new_before)):
                outcome = "progress"
                self.ws.git("add", "-A")
                self.ws.git("commit", "-q", "-m", f"upshift: {summary}"[:200])
                self.state.round_log.append(
                    f"round {n}: {summary} ({before.passed} -> {after.passed} passing, "
                    f"{len(new_after)} new failures left)")
            else:
                outcome = "stall"
                self.state.round_log.append(f"round {n}: no measurable progress. '{summary}'")
            span.set_attribute("upshift.outcome", outcome)
            span.set_attribute("upshift.passed_before", before.passed)
            span.set_attribute("upshift.passed_after", after.passed)
            span.set_attribute("upshift.new_failures_left", len(self.new_failures(after)))
            return after, outcome

    def converse(self, prompt: str) -> str:
        messages = [{"role": "user", "content": [{"text": prompt}]}]
        for _ in range(MAX_STEPS_PER_ROUND):
            response = self.llm.converse(self.system, messages, TOOLS)
            message = response["output"]["message"]
            messages.append(message)
            uses = tool_uses(message)
            if not uses:
                messages.append({"role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Continue with tools, or call finish_round."}]})
                continue
            results, finished = [], None
            for use in uses:
                if "_invalid_json" in use["input"]:
                    tracing.annotate(failure_class="tool_args_invalid_json", recovery="returned_to_model")
                    results.append(tool_result(use["toolUseId"], "Your tool arguments were not valid JSON. "
                                               "Call the tool again with valid JSON.", error=True))
                    continue
                if use["name"] == "finish_round":
                    finished = use["input"].get("summary", "").strip() or "round finished"
                    results.append(tool_result(use["toolUseId"], "ok"))
                    continue
                try:
                    results.append(tool_result(use["toolUseId"], self.call_tool(use["name"], use["input"])))
                except Exception as exc:  # tool errors go back to the model so it can recover
                    tracing.annotate(failure_class=f"tool:{use['name']}", recovery="returned_to_model")
                    results.append(tool_result(use["toolUseId"], f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", error=True))
            messages.append({"role": "user", "content": results})
            if finished:
                return finished
        tracing.annotate(failure_class="step_budget", recovery="end_round")
        return "step budget for the round ran out"

    def call_tool(self, name: str, args: dict) -> str:
        ws = self.ws
        if name == "read_file":
            lines = ws.resolve(args["path"]).read_text().splitlines()
            start = max(args.get("start") or 1, 1)
            end = min(args.get("end") or start + 399, len(lines), start + 399)
            return "\n".join(f"{i:5}  {lines[i - 1]}" for i in range(start, end + 1)) or "(empty file)"

content.text:
v1 is done, with a measured improvement from the trace. Read on the same demo app and model, it costs 17% less ($0.396 → $0.327), uses 26% fewer tokens (193K → 142K), and leaves no deprecated calls, down from 6. Both runs still finish with 16/16 tests passing and no test files touched.

**How neatlogs drove it:** I read the v0 trace through the neatlogs MCP server (`search_traces`, `get_trace_context`). It showed:
- **Duplicate fetches during research:** the model fetched the Pydantic migration page 11 times with different `#anchor`s. Every fetch returned the same 30 KB page, and all of it went into the next model call.
- **A growing fix-loop history:** each of the 10 fix-loop calls resent the whole conversation, including pytest's warnings section every time.
- **A "Slow LLM Response" detection** on the 38-second research call.

**What changed in v1 (20 tests pass):**
- **One fetch per page:** pages are fetched once per conversation, and `#anchor` variants are refused with a short note. v1 made 0 duplicate fetches.
- **Smaller history:** tool outputs older than the last two steps are shortened, and the pytest warnings section is stripped.
- **Cleanup round:** once tests pass, the agent tries to migrate deprecated calls that remain. It commits only if tests still pass and the count drops; otherwise it reverts.
- **Per-round token counts** are now recorded on each fix and cleanup span in neatlogs.
- **`--fresh-research`** makes the comparison fair, since v1 didn't reuse v0's cached research.

**Limits of this evidence:**
- **One run each.** Model output varies between runs, so part of the difference could be luck. Repeating both versions on a few real open-source repos would make the claim solid.
- **The cleanup round never ran for real.** In v1 the model happened to migrate `orders.py` in its first fix round, so cleanup had nothing to do. Only the tests with a scripted model exercise it so far.
- **v0's code exists nowhere now.** Nothing is committed, so v0 can't be re-run for more comparisons. Committing locally now would preserve v1, and doesn't push anything.

Both trace IDs and the full comparison table are in `hackathon.md`. In the neatlogs dashboard, the runs are tagged `v0` and `v1`.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **Event:** the neatHack hackathon (neatlogs.com/hackathon), 48h, Oct 10 12:30 PM to Oct 12 11:55 PM IST. Submission is a quote-tweet on X with team name, project name, public repo and demo.
     - Required tools: neatlogs, Entire (checkpoints / entire-graph) and cfo.ai (business plan).
     - Judging: agent 30%, tool use 25%, demo 20%, building in public 15%, originality 10%.
     - Evidence needed: before/after traces, a recovery trace, Entire checkpoints, a cfo.ai plan, #neatHack posts, and a public repo with commits during the event.
   - **Project:** "Upshift", an agent that fixes the code a version change breaks.
     - Generic, not Pydantic-only.
     - Three triggers:
       - a vulnerability scan (pip-audit, Dependabot optional);
       - a developer-requested bump of a package or the Python version (e.g. 3.10→3.12);
       - third-party API drift auto-detected from logs and neatlogs traces, then the code is updated to the new docs. The demo uses a mock "acme" API.
     - Priority order: engine + bump + vuln first, API drift last.
   - **Models:** for now use our own key (Azure OpenAI). When the product goes live, let users bring their own key from any provider. The user's words: "make sure to never commit that".
   - **Earlier deliverables, all done:**
     - plan file;
     - artifact page https://claude.ai/artifact/GEQJyrwU9sADD7uSffagef;
     - X posts (the latest short version: "Day 1 of #neatHack: building Upshift, an agent that fixes the code a version change breaks. / CVE, Python bump or API sunset: it reads the docs, rewrites the code and proves it with your tests. / Plan done. First real bump next.");
     - infographic `assets/upshift-tools.png` (redesigned: light, colour-blocked, no handle in the footer).
   - **Most recent request:** "yes start the improvement", i.e. v1 improvements driven by neatlogs traces. Before that: "let's wait for the push", so don't push (and nothing has been committed).

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Agent loop:** custom Python. Pipeline phases: setup → baseline → research → bump → fix → verify → report. State is saved between phases (`resume`).
   - **Internal message format:** Bedrock Converse style (text / toolUse / toolResult blocks), translated per provider.
   - **neatlogs SDK 1.4.26:**
     - `neatlogs.init(api_key, workflow_name, tags, disable_export)`
     - `@neatlogs.span(kind=..., tool_name=...)` with kinds WORKFLOW, AGENT, CHAIN, TOOL, RETRIEVER, EMBEDDING, GUARDRAIL, MCP_TOOL
     - `neatlogs.trace(name, kind)` is a context manager that returns a span with `set_attribute`
     - `neatlogs.identify(session_id=)`, `neatlogs.wrap(client)` (supports AzureOpenAI, OpenAI, Anthropic, boto3 bedrock-runtime), `flush`, `shutdown`, `get_delivery_diagnostics`
     - attributes via `opentelemetry.trace.get_current_span()`
   - **neatlogs MCP:** streamable HTTP at https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp with `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Tools include search_traces, get_trace_context (trace_id, offset, created_after), list_detections and triage_*.
   - **Entire CLI 0.11.4:**
     - `entire enable --agent claude-code` installs hooks in `.claude/settings.json` plus git hooks prepare-commit-msg, commit-msg, post-commit, post-rewrite and pre-push.
     - entire-graph plugin v0.4.0: `entire graph search/impact/explain/verify/neighbors/def/...`. Python is a semantic language.
     - `verify --record-baseline/--pre-edit-baseline` needs pytest run with `-rA` or `-v` to parse results.
   - **Research:**
     - PyPI JSON for links and version resolution;
     - GitHub releases API;
     - HTML to text;
     - API diff: install the old and new versions in uv venvs and run `apidiff_probe.py` (uses `__all__` for lazy exports);
     - playbook of cited rules, cached in `playbooks/`, with detect regexes sanitised.
   - **uv** for venvs and installs, Python 3.12 for workspace venvs, pytest run with `python -B` (no .pyc).
   - **Providers:** azure-openai, openai (OPENAI_BASE_URL for any compatible service), bedrock (explicit profile required).
   - **Secret guard:** `scripts/check_secrets.py` as the pre-commit hook. `.gitignore` covers `.env` and `.env.*` except `!.env.example`.

3. Files and Code Sections (repo `/Users/harsh/agent-101/neatlogs-agent`, git remote `https://github.com/harsh-madhav/upshift.git`, 3 pre-existing "first commit" commits; ALL work is uncommitted):
   - **`pyproject.toml`**
     - Project name "upshift", requires-python ≥3.11.
     - Dependencies: boto3, openai, httpx, neatlogs, packaging. Script: `upshift = "upshift.cli:main"`. Dev: pytest. Built with hatchling. testpaths = ["tests"].
   - **`upshift/tracing.py`**
     - `AGENT_VERSION` comes from the `UPSHIFT_AGENT_VERSION` env var.
     - `init(tags)` sets `disable_export` when there is no key.

     - Each class keeps `input_tokens` and `output_tokens` counters.

     - `git()` runs with `-c user.name=upshift -c user.email=upshift@localhost -c commit.gpgsign=false`.
     - `install()`: uv venv, requirements*.txt, then tries `-e .[test,dev]`, `.[test]`, `.[dev]`, `.` in order, plus pytest.
     - Also: `installed_version`, `pin_files`, `set_version` (rewrites pins, then `uv pip install pkg==ver`), `run_tests(selector)` running `[py,"-B","-m","pytest","-q","-rfE","-p","no:cacheprovider","--no-header"]`, `resolve`, `source_files`.

     - `candidate_links`, and `gather(...)` which returns links, docs, release_notes and api_diff.

       ```python
       class Fetcher:
           """Fetch each page at most once per conversation. ..."""
           def __init__(self, cap=SOURCE_CAP, already_read=()):
               self.cap = cap; self.seen = {self.page(u) for u in already_read}; self.duplicates = 0
           @staticmethod
           def page(url): return url.split("#", 1)[0].rstrip("/")
           def __call__(self, url):
               page = self.page(url)
               if page in self.seen:
                   self.duplicates += 1; tracing.annotate(duplicate_fetch=page)
                   return f"[Already fetched {page} earlier in this conversation. A #section anchor does not change the page, so use the text you already have.]"
               self.seen.add(page); return fetch_text(page, cap=self.cap)
       ```

from upshift.workspace import _find_requirement, _rewrite_requirement, parse_pytest


def test_rewrite_pinned_requirement_keeps_pin_style_and_comment():
    text = "requests>=2\npydantic==1.10.13  # models\n"
    assert _rewrite_requirement(text, "pydantic", "2.14.0") == "requests>=2\npydantic==2.14.0  # models\n"


def test_rewrite_keeps_extras_and_markers():
    text = 'pydantic[email]>=1.8,<2; python_version >= "3.8"\n'
    assert _rewrite_requirement(text, "Pydantic", "2.14.0") == \
        'pydantic[email]>=2.14.0; python_version >= "3.8"\n'


def test_rewrite_pyproject_dependency_strings():
    text = '[project]\nname = "shop"\ndependencies = [\n  "pydantic>=1.10,<2",\n  "httpx",\n]\n'
    out = _rewrite_requirement(text, "pydantic", "2.14.0")
    assert '"pydantic>=2.14.0"' in out and '"httpx"' in out and 'name = "shop"' in out


def test_other_packages_untouched():
    text = "pydantic-settings==1.0\npydantic==1.10.13\n"
    assert _rewrite_requirement(text, "pydantic", "2.0") == "pydantic-settings==1.0\npydantic==2.0\n"


def test_find_requirement():
    assert _find_requirement("flask==2.0\n", "Flask")
    assert not _find_requirement("flask-cors==2.0\n", "flask")


def test_parse_pytest_failures_and_collection_errors():
    out = ("FAILED tests/test_a.py::test_one - AssertionError\n"
           "ERROR tests/test_b.py - TypeError: constr() got an unexpected keyword\n"
           "1 failed, 3 passed, 1 error in 0.2s\n")
    run = parse_pytest(1, out)
    assert run.failing == {"tests/test_a.py::test_one", "tests/test_b.py"}
    assert run.passed == 3


def test_fetcher_treats_anchors_as_the_same_page(monkeypatch):
    from upshift import research
    calls = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(research, "fetch_text", lambda url, cap: calls.append(url) or f"page {url}")
    fetch = research.Fetcher(already_read=["https://docs.example.com/changelog/"])
    assert fetch("https://docs.example.com/migration/#config") == "page https://docs.example.com/migration"
    assert "Already fetched" in fetch("https://docs.example.com/migration/#validators")
    assert "Already fetched" in fetch("https://docs.example.com/changelog")
    assert calls == ["https://docs.example.com/migration"] and fetch.duplicates == 2

# neatHack build log: Upshift

## Project
An agent that fixes the code a dependency, Python or third-party API version change breaks.
Three triggers (vulnerability scan, developer-requested bump, API drift seen in traces), one engine:
research → cited playbook → bump → fix loop → verify → report.

## Team
Harsh Gupta

## Stack
- Agent: custom Python loop; bring-your-own-key model layer (Azure OpenAI now, also OpenAI-compatible and Bedrock)
- neatlogs: tracing every job, phase, tool and model call; later also detection of API drift
- Entire: checkpoints for this repo; entire-graph as the agent's search/impact/explain/verify tools
- cfo.ai: business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway), not started

## Build log

### 2026-10-10 (Day 1)
Done:
- Installed Entire 0.11.4 and enabled it for Claude Code, plus the entire-graph plugin (v0.4.0).
  Python is a semantic language in entire-graph.
- Built the package-bump pipeline: setup, baseline, research, bump, fix loop, verify, report, with

"""One job end to end: setup → baseline → research → bump → fix → verify → report.

Each phase is a neatlogs span under the job's WORKFLOW trace, and state is saved between phases.
"""

import re
from pathlib import Path

import neatlogs
from packaging.version import Version

from . import graph, playbook, research, tracing
from .agent import FixLoop
from .llm import make_llm
from .state import RunState
from .workspace import Workspace

REPORT = "UPSHIFT_REPORT.md"


class Stop(Exception):
    """Ends the job early with a message (already at target, dry run, ...)."""


def run(state: RunState, dry_run: bool = False) -> RunState:
    ws = Workspace(state.dir, python=state.python)
    llm = None if dry_run else make_llm()
    with neatlogs.identify(session_id=state.run_id):
        with neatlogs.trace(f"upshift.{state.kind}", kind="WORKFLOW") as root:
            root.set_attribute("upshift.package", state.package)
            root.set_attribute("upshift.repo", state.source)
            root.set_attribute("upshift.run_id", state.run_id)
            try:
                for phase in ("setup", "baseline", "research", "bump", "fix", "verify", "report"):
                    if state.reached(phase):
                        continue
                    with neatlogs.trace(phase, kind="AGENT"):
                        PHASES[phase](state, ws, llm, dry_run)
                    if llm:
                        state.input_tokens, state.output_tokens = llm.input_tokens, llm.output_tokens
                    state.advance(next_phase(phase))
                    print(f"[upshift] {phase} done")
            except Stop as stop:
                state.notes.append(str(stop))
                print(f"[upshift] stopped: {stop}")
            finally:
                root.set_attribute("upshift.phase_reached", state.phase)
                state.save()
    return state


def next_phase(phase: str) -> str:
    order = ["setup", "baseline", "research", "bump", "fix", "verify", "report", "done"]
    return order[order.index(phase) + 1]


def setup(state: RunState, ws: Workspace, llm, dry_run: bool) -> None:
    info = research.pypi_info(state.package)
    state.new = research.resolve_target(info, state.wanted)
    if not ws.repo.exists():
        ws.clone(state.source, f"upshift/{state.kind}-{state.package}-{state.new}")
        state.base_commit = ws.git("rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
    ws.install()
    state.old = ws.installed_version(state.package) or ""
    tracing.annotate(old=state.old, new=state.new)
    if not state.old:
        raise Stop(f"{state.package} is not installed by this project")
    if Version(state.old) >= Version(state.new):
        raise Stop(f"{state.package} is already at {state.old} (target {state.new})")


def baseline(state: RunState, ws: Workspace, llm, dry_run: bool) -> None:
    run = ws.run_tests()
    state.baseline_failing = sorted(run.failing)
    state.baseline_passed = run.passed
    graph.verify(str(ws.repo), ws.test_cmd, record_baseline=str(state.dir / "verify-baseline.json"))
    tracing.annotate(baseline_passed=run.passed, baseline_failing=len(run.failing))


def do_research(state: RunState, ws: Workspace, llm, dry_run: bool) -> None:
    cached = None if state.fresh_research else playbook.load_cached(state.package, state.old, state.new)
    if cached:
        state.playbook_path = str(playbook.cache_path(state.package, state.old, state.new))
        tracing.annotate(playbook_cache="hit")
        return
    tracing.annotate(playbook_cache="miss")
    sources = research.gather(state.package, state.old, state.new, state.python, state.dir)
    (state.dir / "sources.md").write_text(playbook.render_sources(sources))
    if dry_run:
        return
    state.playbook_path = str(playbook.save(playbook.build(llm, sources)))


def bump(state: RunState, ws: Workspace, llm, dry_run: bool) -> None:
    ws.set_version(state.package, state.new)
    ws.git("add", "-A")
    ws.git("commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", f"upshift: bump {state.package} {state.old} -> {state.new}")
    if dry_run:
        run = ws.run_tests()
        new = sorted(run.failing - set(state.baseline_failing))
        (state.dir / "after-bump.txt").write_text(run.output)
        raise Stop(f"dry run: after the bump {run.passed} pass, {len(new)} new failures "
                   f"(sources in {state.dir / 'sources.md'}, pytest output in {state.dir / 'after-bump.txt'})")


def fix(state: RunState, ws: Workspace, llm, dry_run: bool) -> None:
    pb = playbook.load(state.playbook_path)
    loop = FixLoop(ws, llm, state, pb)
    final = loop.run(state.save)
    if not loop.new_failures(final):
        loop.cleanup(lambda: leftover_usages(ws, pb), state.save)


def verify(state: RunState, ws: Workspace, llm, dry_run: bool) -> None:
    run = ws.run_tests()
    new_failures = sorted(run.failing - set(state.baseline_failing))
    verdict = graph.verify(str(ws.repo), ws.test_cmd, pre_edit_baseline=str(state.dir / "verify-baseline.json"))
    leftovers = leftover_usages(ws, playbook.load(state.playbook_path))
    state.result = {
        "passed": run.passed,
        "baseline_passed": state.baseline_passed,
        "new_failures": new_failures,
        "leftover_old_apis": leftovers,
        "entire_verdict": verdict,
        "ok": not new_failures,
    }
    tracing.annotate(ok=not new_failures, new_failures=len(new_failures), leftovers=len(leftovers))


def is_test_file(rel: Path) -> bool:
    return "tests" in rel.parts or "test" in rel.parts or rel.name.startswith("test_") or rel.name == "conftest.py"


def leftover_usages(ws: Workspace, pb: dict, limit: int = 50) -> list[str]:
    """Non-test source lines that still use an old API from the playbook."""
    hits = []
    patterns = []
    for rule in pb["rules"]:
        if not rule.get("detect"):
            continue
        try:
            patterns.append((re.compile(rule["detect"]), rule["why"]))
        except re.error:
            continue
    for path in sorted(ws.source_files()):
        rel = path.relative_to(ws.repo)
        if path.suffix != ".py" or is_test_file(rel):
            continue
        for i, line in enumerate(path.read_text(errors="ignore").splitlines(), 1):
            for regex, why in patterns:
                if regex.search(line):
                    hits.append(f"{rel}:{i} `{line.strip()}`: {why}")
                    break
                    if len(hits) >= limit:
                        return hits
    return hits


def report(state: RunState, ws: Workspace, llm, dry_run: bool) -> None:
    r = state.result
    pb = playbook.load(state.playbook_path)
    diffstat = ws.git("diff", "--stat", state.base_commit, "HEAD").strip().splitlines()
    lines = [
        f"# Upshift: {state.package} {state.old} → {state.new}",
        "",
        f"**Result:** {'no new test failures' if r['ok'] else str(len(r['new_failures'])) + ' new test failures remain'}"
        f" · {r['passed']} passing (baseline {r['baseline_passed']})",
        f"**Run:** `{state.run_id}` · {state.round} fix rounds · "
        f"{state.input_tokens:,} input / {state.output_tokens:,} output tokens",
        "",
        "## What changed",
        *[f"- {entry}" for entry in state.round_log],
        "",
        f"`{diffstat[-1].strip() if diffstat else 'no diff'}`",
        "",
        "## Verification (entire graph verify against the pre-upgrade baseline)",
        "```", r["entire_verdict"].strip(), "```",
    ]
    if r["new_failures"]:
        lines += ["", "## Still failing", *[f"- `{t}`" for t in r["new_failures"]]]
    if r["leftover_old_apis"]:
        lines += ["", "## Old APIs still in use", *[f"- {h}" for h in r["leftover_old_apis"]]]
    lines += ["", "## Playbook", pb.get("summary", ""), "",
              *[f"- `{x['old']}` → `{x['new']}` — {x['why']} ([source]({x['source']}))"
                if x["source"].startswith("http") else f"- `{x['old']}` → `{x['new']}` — {x['why']} (API diff)"
                for x in pb["rules"]]]
    if state.notes:
        lines += ["", "## Notes", *[f"- {n}" for n in state.notes]]
    text = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    (ws.repo / REPORT).write_text(text)
    (state.dir / REPORT).write_text(text)
    ws.git("add", REPORT)
    ws.git("commit", "-q", "-m", f"upshift: report for {state.package} {state.new}")


PHASES = {"setup": setup, "baseline": baseline, "research": do_research, "bump": bump,
          "fix": fix, "verify": verify, "report": report}

95	    ws.set_version(state.package, state.new)
96	    ws.git("add", "-A")
97	    ws.git("commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", f"upshift: bump {state.package} {state.old} -> {state.new}")
98	    if dry_run:
99	        run = ws.run_tests()
100	        new = sorted(run.failing - set(state.baseline_failing))
101	        (state.dir / "after-bump.txt").write_text(run.output)
102	        raise Stop(f"dry run: after the bump {run.passed} pass, {len(new)} new failures "
103	                   f"(sources in {state.dir / 'sources.md'}, pytest output in {state.dir / 'after-bump.txt'})")

106	def fix(state: RunState, ws: Workspace, llm, dry_run: bool) -> None:
107	    pb = playbook.load(state.playbook_path)

109	    final = loop.run(state.save)

114	def verify(state: RunState, ws: Workspace, llm, dry_run: bool) -> None:
115	    run = ws.run_tests()

117	    verdict = graph.verify(str(ws.repo), ws.test_cmd, pre_edit_baseline=str(state.dir / "verify-baseline.json"))
118	    leftovers = leftover_usages(ws, playbook.load(state.playbook_path))

135	    """Non-test source lines that still use an old API from the playbook."""
136	    hits = []
137	    patterns = []
138	    for rule in pb["rules"]:

150	            for regex, why in patterns:

154	                    if len(hits) >= limit:

185	                if x["source"].startswith("http") else f"- `{x['old']}` → `{x['new']}` — {x['why']} (API diff)"

from types import SimpleNamespace as NS

import pytest

from upshift.llm import LLMConfigError, from_openai, make_llm, openai_tool, to_openai, tool_result, tool_spec


def test_tool_spec_becomes_openai_function():
    spec = tool_spec("read_file", "Read a file.", {"path": {"type": "string"}}, ["path"])
    assert openai_tool(spec) == {"type": "function", "function": {
        "name": "read_file", "description": "Read a file.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["path"]}}}


def test_conversation_round_trip_to_openai():
    messages = [
        {"role": "user", "content": [{"text": "fix it"}]},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": [
            {"text": "reading"},
            {"toolUse": {"toolUseId": "c1", "name": "read_file", "input": {"path": "a.py"}}}]},
        {"role": "user", "content": [tool_result("c1", "no such file", error=True)]},
    ]
    assert to_openai("sys", messages) == [
        {"role": "system", "content": "sys"},
        {"role": "user", "content": "fix it"},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": "reading", "tool_calls": [
            {"id": "c1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "read_file", "arguments": '{"path": "a.py"}'}}]},
        {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "c1", "content": "ERROR: no such file"},
    ]


def test_openai_reply_becomes_tool_use_blocks():
    reply = NS(content=None, tool_calls=[
        NS(id="c2", function=NS(name="edit_file", arguments='{"path": "a.py", "old": "x", "new": "y"}')),
        NS(id="c3", function=NS(name="run_tests", arguments="{not json")),
    ])
    message = from_openai(reply)
    assert message["content"][0]["toolUse"] == {
        "toolUseId": "c2", "name": "edit_file", "input": {"path": "a.py", "old": "x", "new": "y"}}
    assert "_invalid_json" in message["content"][1]["toolUse"]["input"]


def test_provider_must_be_chosen(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.delenv("UPSHIFT_PROVIDER", raising=False)
    with pytest.raises(LLMConfigError):
        make_llm()


def test_azure_needs_its_settings(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("UPSHIFT_PROVIDER", "azure-openai")
    monkeypatch.setenv("UPSHIFT_MODEL", "my-deployment")
    monkeypatch.delenv("AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY", raising=False)
    monkeypatch.delenv("AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT", raising=False)
    with pytest.raises(LLMConfigError, match="AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY"):
        make_llm()


def test_playbook_drops_detect_patterns_that_match_new_code():
    from upshift.playbook import sanitize
    pb = sanitize({"rules": [
        {"old": "m.dict()", "new": "m.model_dump()", "detect": r"\.dict\(", "why": "", "source": ""},
        {"old": "assert M(x=1) == {'x': 1}", "new": "assert M(x=1).model_dump() == {'x': 1}",
         "detect": r"==\s*\{", "why": "", "source": ""},
        {"old": "x", "new": "y", "detect": "([", "why": "", "source": ""},
    ]})
    assert [r["detect"] for r in pb["rules"]] == [r"\.dict\(", "", ""]

"""Turn research into a cited migration playbook. Cached so the next repo skips research."""

import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

import neatlogs

from . import tracing
from .llm import text_of, tool_result, tool_spec, tool_uses
from .research import Fetcher

CACHE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "playbooks"
MAX_TURNS = 10

SYSTEM = """You research Python dependency upgrades and write migration playbooks.

You get the package, the old and new versions, the project's doc and changelog pages, GitHub release
notes between the versions, and an API diff computed by installing both versions and comparing their
public symbols. The API diff is ground truth for what was removed or changed.

Read what you were given. If you need the official migration guide or a specific doc page, use
fetch_url (follow links you saw, don't guess random URLs). Each page is returned whole, so fetch a
page once; #section anchors return the same page. Then call submit_playbook once.

Each rule must describe one concrete breaking change a codebase could hit, as:
- old: the old usage, written as code
- new: what to write instead, as code
- detect: a Python regex that matches the old usage and never matches correct new-version code, or ""
  for behavioural changes that can't be found textually
- why: one sentence
- source: the URL you read it in, or "api-diff"
Only include rules supported by a source. Prefer 10-40 high-value rules over exhaustive lists."""

TOOLS = [
    tool_spec("fetch_url", "Fetch a web page as text (docs, migration guide, changelog).",
              {"url": {"type": "string"}}, ["url"]),
    tool_spec("submit_playbook", "Submit the finished playbook.", {
        "summary": {"type": "string", "description": "2-4 sentences on the shape of this upgrade."},
        "rules": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object", "properties": {
            "old": {"type": "string"}, "new": {"type": "string"}, "detect": {"type": "string"},
            "why": {"type": "string"}, "source": {"type": "string"}},
            "required": ["old", "new", "detect", "why", "source"]}},
    }, ["summary", "rules"]),
]


def cache_path(package: str, old: str, new: str) -> Path:
    return CACHE / f"{package.lower()}-{old}-{new}.json"


def load_cached(package: str, old: str, new: str) -> dict | None:
    path = cache_path(package, old, new)
    return load(path) if path.exists() else None


def load(path: str | Path) -> dict:
    return sanitize(json.loads(Path(path).read_text()))


def sanitize(playbook: dict) -> dict:
    """Keep a rule's detect regex only if it matches the rule's old example and not its new one.

    Models sometimes write patterns like `==\\s*\\{` that flag valid code everywhere.
    """
    for rule in playbook["rules"]:
        pattern = rule.get("detect") or ""
        try:
            ok = bool(pattern) and re.search(pattern, rule["old"]) and not re.search(pattern, rule["new"])
        except re.error:
            ok = False
        rule["detect"] = pattern if ok else ""
    return playbook


def render_sources(sources: dict) -> str:
    docs = "\n\n".join(f"### {name}\n{text}" for name, text in sources["docs"].items())
    links = "\n".join(f"- {k}: {v}" for k, v in sources["links"].items())
    return (f"Package: {sources['package']}  {sources['old']} -> {sources['new']}\n\n"
            f"## Project links\n{links}\n\n## Doc and changelog pages\n{docs or '(none)'}\n\n"
            f"## GitHub release notes in range\n{sources['release_notes']}\n\n"
            f"## API diff (installed both versions)\n{sources['api_diff']}")


@neatlogs.span(kind="AGENT", name="playbook")
def build(llm, sources: dict) -> dict:
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": [{"text": render_sources(sources)}]}]
    fetch = Fetcher(already_read=[sources["links"][name] for name in sources["docs"] if name in sources["links"]])
    for _ in range(MAX_TURNS):
        response = llm.converse(SYSTEM, messages, TOOLS, max_tokens=16000)
        message = response["output"]["message"]
        messages.append(message)
        uses = tool_uses(message)
        if not uses:
            messages.append({"role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Call submit_playbook with your rules."}]})
            continue
        results = []
        for use in uses:
            if "_invalid_json" in use["input"]:
                results.append(tool_result(use["toolUseId"], "Arguments were not valid JSON; call again.", error=True))
                continue
            if use["name"] == "submit_playbook":
                playbook = sanitize({"package": sources["package"], "old": sources["old"],
                                     "new": sources["new"], **use["input"]})
                tracing.annotate(playbook_rules=len(playbook["rules"]), urls_fetched=len(fetch.seen),
                                 duplicate_fetches_refused=fetch.duplicates)
                return playbook
            if use["name"] == "fetch_url":
                results.append(tool_result(use["toolUseId"], fetch(use["input"]["url"])))
            else:
                results.append(tool_result(use["toolUseId"], f"unknown tool {use['name']}", error=True))
        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": results})
    raise RuntimeError(f"no playbook after {MAX_TURNS} turns; last reply: {text_of(messages[-1])[:500]}")


def save(playbook: dict) -> Path:
    CACHE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    path = cache_path(playbook["package"], playbook["old"], playbook["new"])
    path.write_text(json.dumps(playbook, indent=2))
    return path


def render(playbook: dict) -> str:
    lines = [playbook.get("summary", "")]
    for i, rule in enumerate(playbook["rules"], 1):
        lines.append(f"R{i}. {rule['old']}  =>  {rule['new']}   ({rule['why']}; source: {rule['source']})")
    return "\n".join(lines)

# neatHack plan: autonomous dependency & API upkeep agent (working name `upshift`)

## Context
neatHack (48h, Oct 10 12:30 PM → Oct 12 11:55 PM IST) asks for an agent that completes a substantial task end-to-end. It must use **neatlogs**, **Entire** and **cfo.ai**, with checkable evidence for each. Judging: agent 30%, tool use 25%, demo 20%, building in public 15%, originality 10%.

**What the agent does:** it keeps a Python repo current, fixing the code that breaks, not just opening bump PRs the way Dependabot does. **One engine, three triggers:**

| Trigger | Detects | Researches | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Vuln** | `pip-audit` (OSV) JSON; Dependabot alerts via `gh api` when the repo is on GitHub | Advisory + changelog between versions | jinja2 CVE → fixed version |
| **Bump** (developer asks) | `upshift bump --package X --to Y` or `--python 3.12` | Package: PyPI links, changelog, releases, API diff. Python: "What's New" per minor version, removed stdlib modules, dependency compatibility | Pydantic 1→2; Python 3.10→3.12 |
| **API drift** | App logs + neatlogs traces: `Deprecation`/`Sunset`/`Link: rel=successor-version` headers, 410/4xx bursts, "deprecated" warnings | The provider's new docs / OpenAPI spec, diffed against the old one | acme API v1 → v2 |

Every trigger produces a **Job** that goes through the same pipeline: **research → cited playbook → plan → fix loop → recover → verify → branch + PR**.

**Decisions made:**
- Claude on **Bedrock** (AWS credits)
- Custom Python loop
- Python ecosystem only
- Priority: engine + bump + vuln first, API drift last
- Logs: neatlogs traces + local log files
- API-drift demo: a mock API we control
- Vuln source: pip-audit, with Dependabot optional

`/Users/harsh/agent-101/neatlogs-agent` is empty, so this is greenfield. It must become a **public** repo with commits dated inside the event. The repo name is open (see the end).

---

## Pipeline (shared engine)
CLI commands:
- `upshift scan --repo R` (vuln)
- `upshift bump --repo R (--package P [--to V] | --python 3.12)`
- `upshift watch --repo R [--logs PATH] [--neatlogs]` (API drift)
- `upshift resume <run_id>`
- `upshift bench`

1. **Trigger → Job** `{kind, target, evidence}`.
   - **Vuln:** pick the *smallest* fixed version, preferring the same major version. Only a major jump goes through the full migration path.
   - **Python bump:** run `uv pip compile --python-version 3.12` to find dependencies that won't resolve. Each becomes a sub-job through the same engine.
2. **Research → playbook.** A list of rules (old pattern → new pattern), each with its source URL, cached in `playbooks/`.
   - **Package:** PyPI JSON → changelog/docs/source links → migration guide and release notes. An **API diff** installs both versions in temp venvs (`uv`) and compares public symbols and signatures with `inspect`. It's the ground truth when docs are thin.
   - **Python:** `docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.11.html`, `3.12.html`, and so on. Removed modules (`distutils`, `imp`, `asynchat`…). Config surfaces to update: `requires-python`, `.python-version`, Dockerfile `FROM`, CI matrix, tox.
   - **API:** follow the `Link` successor URL / configured docs URL → fetch the old and new OpenAPI specs → diff endpoints, params, fields and auth headers.
3. **Setup.** Clone into `workspaces/<run_id>`, then `uv venv` (with the target Python if needed) and install. Record the test baseline with `entire graph verify --test "pytest -q" --record-baseline`.
4. **Plan.** Find affected code with `entire graph search`/`symbols` plus grep for playbook APIs (for API drift: the host/URL/client methods). Order the work by blast radius with `entire graph impact`.
5. **Apply the bump / config change**, run the tests, and group the failures by root cause.
6. **Fix loop** (Claude tool-use, one failure group at a time). Tools: `read_file`, `edit_file`, `run_tests`, `graph_impact`, `graph_explain`, `search_code`, `lookup_playbook` and `fetch_docs`. New findings are added back to the playbook. A group that passes is committed; a regression means reverting that file.
7. **Recover.** Classify each failure and pick a strategy:
   - Bedrock throttle → backoff and retry.
   - Bad edit → re-read the file and retry.
   - Regression → revert and re-plan with the error in context.
   - Install conflict → relax or pin, or spawn a sub-job.
   - Budget cap (iterations, tokens, $) → stop with a partial report.
8. **State.** Write `.upshift/state.json` and make a git commit per fixed group, so `resume` survives a crash or kill.
9. **Verify** (a `GUARDRAIL` span).
   - `entire graph verify --pre-edit-baseline` must report no new failures.
   - Vuln: `pip-audit` is clean for that advisory.
   - Bump: tests run with deprecation warnings as errors, and no old APIs from the playbook remain.
   - API drift: tests pass against the new API version, and a re-run shows no deprecation signals.
10. **Output.** A branch `upshift/<kind>-<target>`, `UPSHIFT_REPORT.md` (changes, playbook citations, what's left, cost) and a PR body (`gh pr create` is optional).

## Demo setup (one story, all three triggers)
- **`demo/acme_api/`**: a FastAPI mock third-party API.
  - `/v1/charges` has modes `ok → deprecating → sunset`. "Deprecating" sends `Deprecation`, `Sunset` and `Link` headers; "sunset" returns 410.
  - `/v2/payments` renames fields (`amount` → `amount_cents`), requires an `Idempotency-Key` header, and nests the response.
  - It serves `/v1/openapi.json`, `/v2/openapi.json` and `/docs/migration`.
- **`demo/shop_app/`**: a deliberately neglected app.
  - Python 3.10, vulnerable pins (e.g. old jinja2/werkzeug), Pydantic v1, and calls to acme v1.
  - Instrumented with neatlogs (acme calls wrapped as `TOOL` spans that record status codes and headers), writing to `logs/app.log`.
  - Has pytest tests that run against the mock.
- **Demo flow:** `scan` fixes the CVEs → `bump --python 3.12` → put the mock in "deprecating" mode and run the app → `watch` sees the drift in neatlogs and the logs, then migrates to v2 → switch the mock to "sunset" mode and the app still works.
- **`evals/repos.yaml`**: shop_app plus 3–4 small real OSS repos (Pydantic 1→2, SQLAlchemy 1.4→2.0, one Python bump), pinned to fixed commits.

## Files to create
```
pyproject.toml                       # neatlogs[anthropic], boto3, mcp, pip-audit, typer, pyyaml, httpx
upshift/cli.py                       # scan | bump | watch | resume | bench
upshift/jobs.py                      # Job model
upshift/triggers/{vuln,bump,api_drift}.py
upshift/research/{package,python,api,playbook}.py
upshift/engine/{agent,tools,recovery,state}.py
upshift/llm.py                       # Bedrock Converse wrapper (model id via env)
upshift/graph.py                     # subprocess wrappers over `entire graph ...`
upshift/neatlogs_mcp.py              # MCP client → search_traces / list_detections / get_trace_context
upshift/prompts/
playbooks/                           # cached cited playbooks
demo/acme_api/, demo/shop_app/
evals/repos.yaml, evals/bench.py
business/                            # cfo.ai export
hackathon.md, README.md              # build log + evidence table
```

---

## How each required tool is used

### neatlogs: observe and improve the agent, *and* a detection source
1. **Tracing the agent.**
   - `neatlogs.init(workflow_name="upshift", tags=[agent_version, job_kind, repo], instrumentations=["bedrock"])` before importing boto3.
   - Spans: `WORKFLOW` per job, `AGENT` per phase (research/plan/fix/verify), `TOOL` per tool (including every `entire graph` call), `GUARDRAIL` for verify.
   - `set_attribute` for state transitions, failure class, retries and recovery strategy.
   - `identify` sets session = run_id, so resumed runs stay together.
   - `flush()`/`shutdown()` on exit.
2. **Detection for API drift.** The agent is an **MCP client of neatlogs** (`https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp`). It calls `search_traces` / `list_detections` / `get_trace_context` on the shop_app project to find failing or deprecated acme calls, and falls back to local logs. This matches the hackathon's "watch a running system" example.
3. **Improvement loop.**
   - Run `bench` as v0.
   - In Claude Code, use the neatlogs MCP (`triage_list`, `get_trace_context`, `list_detections`) to find waste and failure patterns. Fix them, then run v1.
   - Compare success rate, iterations, tokens, $ per job and wall time.
4. **Recovery evidence** comes from real failure traces (throttles, bad edits, regressions, install conflicts).
5. **Unit cost** per job type, as measured in neatlogs, feeds cfo.ai.

### Entire: context for us *and* the agent
1. **On our repo.**
   - `entire enable --agent claude-code` adds checkpoint trailers that link each commit to the Claude Code session that wrote it. This is the evidence, and it proves the code was written during the event.
   - `entire graph init-agents` gives Claude Code graph guidance while we build.
2. **Inside the agent.** entire-graph is its code-intelligence layer:
   - `search`/`symbols` → find usages of the affected APIs and third-party call sites
   - `impact`/`neighbors` → order fixes by blast radius
   - `explain` → pipe pytest failures in to get the relevant declarations
   - `verify` with record/pre-edit baselines → the verification gate

### cfo.ai: the business plan
1. Model "autonomous dependency & API upkeep" with Ari:
   - **Pricing:** per-repo/month subscription plus per-job overage for major migrations.
   - **COGS:** neatlogs $ per job type plus compute.
   - **Opex/headcount**, base/upside **revenue scenarios**, **runway**.
   - **Positioning:** Dependabot/Renovate open bump PRs but leave the breakage to you. Snyk fixes vulnerabilities only. Upshift fixes the code, including drift in runtime APIs.
2. Share a read-only page link and export to `business/plan.md`. Cancel cfo.ai billing right after signup.

---

## Evidence table (README)
| Claim | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Agent improved | v0 vs v1 neatlogs trace links + bench table |
| Used neatlogs | trace links, the agent's MCP detection calls, MCP-driven fixes logged in `hackathon.md` |
| Used Entire | `entire checkpoint list`, commit trailers, graph `TOOL` spans in traces |
| Used cfo.ai | `business/plan.md` + shared page link |
| Recovers from failures | a specific recovery trace link |
| Built in public | #neatHack posts |
| Written during hackathon | public repo, commit dates |

- **Oct 10 (today).**
  - Credits and AWS check-in; public repo; `entire enable`; neatlogs init.
  - Check the risks below.
  - Engine end-to-end on **one manual package bump** (Pydantic, on 1 repo), in rough v0 form. Post #1.

- **Oct 11, afternoon/evening.**
  - **API drift:** acme mock, shop_app, log + neatlogs MCP detection, OpenAPI diff → fix.
  - v0 bench → neatlogs analysis → v1.
  - cfo.ai plan. Post #3.
- **Oct 12 (until ~6 PM).** v1 bench, README evidence, ~3-minute video (the demo flow above plus traces plus cfo.ai). Submit 7:00–11:55 PM.
- **Cut line:** if API drift isn't working by Oct 11 at 9 PM, use local-log detection only (drop the neatlogs MCP detection) and demo only the "deprecating" mode.

## Risks to check first
- How well entire-graph handles Python (`entire graph capabilities --json`). Fallback: grep + `ast` for search/impact.
- Whether neatlogs `bedrock` auto-instrumentation catches boto3 `converse`. Fallback: `neatlogs.wrap(client)`.
- Whether the neatlogs MCP can search non-LLM `TOOL` spans by attribute (status code/headers) for shop_app. Fallback: local logs.
- Bedrock model access/region (env-configurable). `uv python install 3.12` works offline-ish.
- Huge changelogs. Cap text per source, rely on the API/OpenAPI diff as truth, and cite every rule.

## Verification
- `upshift scan --repo demo/shop_app` → `pip-audit` comes back clean for the fixed advisories, with no new test failures.
- `upshift bump --repo demo/shop_app --python 3.12` → tests pass in a 3.12 venv; `requires-python`, Dockerfile and CI are updated.
- `upshift bump --package pydantic --to 2` on bench repos → `entire graph verify --pre-edit-baseline` shows zero new failures. At least 2 different frameworks pass with no framework-specific code.
- Mock in "deprecating" mode → run shop_app → `upshift watch --neatlogs` detects acme v1 → migrates to v2 → tests pass against v2. With the mock in "sunset" mode, the app still works.
- Kill mid-run, then `upshift resume <id>` → finishes without redoing completed groups.
- neatlogs shows WORKFLOW→AGENT→TOOL spans with tokens and cost, and v0/v1 can be filtered by tag. `git log` has `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers.

## Repo name (open)
Not prescribed by the hackathon. Still fits: **`upshift`** (recommended), `bumpbot`, `keepcurrent`, `driftfix`.

  - `/v2/payments` renames fields (`amount` → `amount_cents`), requires an `Idempotency-Key` header, and nests the response.
  - It serves `/v1/openapi.json`, `/v2/openapi.json` and `/docs/migration`.
- **`demo/shop_app/`**: a deliberately neglected app.
  - Python 3.10, vulnerable pins (e.g. old jinja2/werkzeug), Pydantic v1, and calls to acme v1.
  - Instrumented with neatlogs (acme calls wrapped as `TOOL` spans that record status codes and headers), writing to `logs/app.log`.
  - Has pytest tests that run against the mock.
- **Demo flow:** `scan` fixes the CVEs → `bump --python 3.12` → put the mock in "deprecating" mode and run the app → `watch` sees the drift in neatlogs and the logs, then migrates to v2 → switch the mock to "sunset" mode and the app still works.
- **`evals/repos.yaml`**: shop_app plus 3–4 small real OSS repos (Pydantic 1→2, SQLAlchemy 1.4→2.0, one Python bump), pinned to fixed commits.

## Files to create
```
pyproject.toml                       # neatlogs[anthropic], boto3, mcp, pip-audit, typer, pyyaml, httpx
upshift/cli.py                       # scan | bump | watch | resume | bench
upshift/jobs.py                      # Job model
upshift/triggers/{vuln,bump,api_drift}.py
upshift/research/{package,python,api,playbook}.py
upshift/engine/{agent,tools,recovery,state}.py
upshift/llm.py                       # Bedrock Converse wrapper (model id via env)
upshift/graph.py                     # subprocess wrappers over `entire graph ...`
upshift/neatlogs_mcp.py              # MCP client → search_traces / list_detections / get_trace_context
upshift/prompts/
playbooks/                           # cached cited playbooks
demo/acme_api/, demo/shop_app/
evals/repos.yaml, evals/bench.py
business/                            # cfo.ai export
hackathon.md, README.md              # build log + evidence table
```

---

## How each required tool is used

### neatlogs: observe and improve the agent, *and* a detection source
1. **Tracing the agent.**
   - `neatlogs.init(workflow_name="upshift", tags=[agent_version, job_kind, repo], instrumentations=["bedrock"])` before importing boto3.
   - Spans: `WORKFLOW` per job, `AGENT` per phase (research/plan/fix/verify), `TOOL` per tool (including every `entire graph` call), `GUARDRAIL` for verify.
   - `set_attribute` for state transitions, failure class, retries and recovery strategy.
   - `identify` sets session = run_id, so resumed runs stay together.
   - `flush()`/`shutdown()` on exit.
2. **Detection for API drift.** The agent is an **MCP client of neatlogs** (`https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp`). It calls `search_traces` / `list_detections` / `get_trace_context` on the shop_app project to find failing or deprecated acme calls, and falls back to local logs. This matches the hackathon's "watch a running system" example.
3. **Improvement loop.**
   - Run `bench` as v0.
   - In Claude Code, use the neatlogs MCP (`triage_list`, `get_trace_context`, `list_detections`) to find waste and failure patterns. Fix them, then run v1.
   - Compare success rate, iterations, tokens, $ per job and wall time.
4. **Recovery evidence** comes from real failure traces (throttles, bad edits, regressions, install conflicts).
5. **Unit cost** per job type, as measured in neatlogs, feeds cfo.ai.

### Entire: context for us *and* the agent
1. **On our repo.**
   - `entire enable --agent claude-code` adds checkpoint trailers that link each commit to the Claude Code session that wrote it. This is the evidence, and it proves the code was written during the event.
   - `entire graph init-agents` gives Claude Code graph guidance while we build.
2. **Inside the agent.** entire-graph is its code-intelligence layer:
   - `search`/`symbols` → find usages of the affected APIs and third-party call sites
   - `impact`/`neighbors` → order fixes by blast radius
   - `explain` → pipe pytest failures in to get the relevant declarations
   - `verify` with record/pre-edit baselines → the verification gate

### cfo.ai: the business plan
1. Model "autonomous dependency & API upkeep" with Ari:
   - **Pricing:** per-repo/month subscription plus per-job overage for major migrations.
   - **COGS:** neatlogs $ per job type plus compute.
   - **Opex/headcount**, base/upside **revenue scenarios**, **runway**.
   - **Positioning:** Dependabot/Renovate open bump PRs but leave the breakage to you. Snyk fixes vulnerabilities only. Upshift fixes the code, including drift in runtime APIs.
2. Share a read-only page link and export to `business/plan.md`. Cancel cfo.ai billing right after signup.

---

## Evidence table (README)
| Claim | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Agent improved | v0 vs v1 neatlogs trace links + bench table |
| Used neatlogs | trace links, the agent's MCP detection calls, MCP-driven fixes logged in `hackathon.md` |
| Used Entire | `entire checkpoint list`, commit trailers, graph `TOOL` spans in traces |
| Used cfo.ai | `business/plan.md` + shared page link |
| Recovers from failures | a specific recovery trace link |
| Built in public | #neatHack posts |
| Written during hackathon | public repo, commit dates |

## Timeline (IST) and cut line
- **Oct 10 (today).**
  - Credits and AWS check-in; public repo; `entire enable`; neatlogs init.
  - Check the risks below.
  - Engine end-to-end on **one manual package bump** (Pydantic, on 1 repo), in rough v0 form. Post #1.
- **Oct 11, morning.** Recovery, state/resume, verify gate. **Vuln trigger** (pip-audit → Job). **Python bump** (uv + whatsnew + dependency sub-jobs). Post #2.
- **Oct 11, afternoon/evening.**
  - **API drift:** acme mock, shop_app, log + neatlogs MCP detection, OpenAPI diff → fix.
  - v0 bench → neatlogs analysis → v1.
  - cfo.ai plan. Post #3.
- **Oct 12 (until ~6 PM).** v1 bench, README evidence, ~3-minute video (the demo flow above plus traces plus cfo.ai). Submit 7:00–11:55 PM.
- **Cut line:** if API drift isn't working by Oct 11 at 9 PM, use local-log detection only (drop the neatlogs MCP detection) and demo only the "deprecating" mode.

## Risks to check first
- How well entire-graph handles Python (`entire graph capabilities --json`). Fallback: grep + `ast` for search/impact.
- Whether neatlogs `bedrock` auto-instrumentation catches boto3 `converse`. Fallback: `neatlogs.wrap(client)`.
- Whether the neatlogs MCP can search non-LLM `TOOL` spans by attribute (status code/headers) for shop_app. Fallback: local logs.
- Bedrock model access/region (env-configurable). `uv python install 3.12` works offline-ish.
- Huge changelogs. Cap text per source, rely on the API/OpenAPI diff as truth, and cite every rule.

## Verification
- `upshift scan --repo demo/shop_app` → `pip-audit` comes back clean for the fixed advisories, with no new test failures.
- `upshift bump --repo demo/shop_app --python 3.12` → tests pass in a 3.12 venv; `requires-python`, Dockerfile and CI are updated.
- `upshift bump --package pydantic --to 2` on bench repos → `entire graph verify --pre-edit-baseline` shows zero new failures. At least 2 different frameworks pass with no framework-specific code.
- Mock in "deprecating" mode → run shop_app → `upshift watch --neatlogs` detects acme v1 → migrates to v2 → tests pass against v2. With the mock in "sunset" mode, the app still works.
- Kill mid-run, then `upshift resume <id>` → finishes without redoing completed groups.
- neatlogs shows WORKFLOW→AGENT→TOOL spans with tokens and cost, and v0/v1 can be filtered by tag. `git log` has `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers.

## Repo name (open)
Not prescribed by the hackathon. Still fits: **`upshift`** (recommended), `bumpbot`, `keepcurrent`, `driftfix`.


If this plan is relevant to the current work and not already complete, continue working on it.
</system-reminder>

Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). # CLAUDE.md

Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.

**Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.

## 1. Think Before Coding

**Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**

Before implementing:
- State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
- If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
- If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
- If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.

## 2. Simplicity First

**Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**

- No features beyond what was asked.
- No abstractions for single-use code.
- No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
- No error handling for impossible scenarios.
- If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.

Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.

## 3. Surgical Changes

**Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**

When editing existing code:
- Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
- Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
- Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
- If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.

When your changes create orphans:
- Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
- Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.

The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.

## 4. Goal-Driven Execution

**Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**

Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
- "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
- "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
- "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"

For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
```
1. [Step] → verify: [check]
2. [Step] → verify: [check]
3. [Step] → verify: [check]
```

Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.

---

**These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

When the user types `/graphify`, invoke the Skill tool with `skill: "graphify"` before doing anything else.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

entries.name: ExitPlanMode
entries.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.
